title: intern-conversion-30day-activation-and-eval-canvas (WIP)
summary: Working canvas to increase intern-to-fulltime conversion velocity while standardizing evidence collection and first-30-day activation. Emphasis on buddy rotations, micro-project deliverables, and a lightweight rubric for conversion decisions.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical playbook for converting interns (sourced via university programs, hackathons, or referrals) into IC hires. It blends a hiring-plan mindset (how we decide to convert), an interview/evaluation rubric (evidence we collect), and a week-1 / 30-day activation checklist (how to set them up to succeed).

Goals:
- Raise intern-to-offer conversion quality while shortening decision time to <= 10 working days after final demo.
- Standardize evidence gathered during internship so hiring decisions map to on-the-job signals.
- Reduce manager friction by shipping a repeatable mentor/buddy schedule and evaluation template.

Key conversion funnel (metrics to track):
- Accepts into program -> Active intern (first 3 days onboarded) -> Project demo submitted by week 8 -> Hiring recommendation queued -> Offer extended.
- Target metrics: Demo submission rate >= 92%, Hiring recommendation decisions within 10 days of demo, Offer acceptance >= 60% for conversion candidates.

Stakeholders:
- Hiring decision: manager + 2 cross-functional reviewers (mentor + product/PM rep).
- People Ops: coordinates offers, equity/salary bands, onboarding logistics.
- Mentors: weekly 1:1 and shadow rotation hosts.

Mentor pairing matrix (practical):
- Lead mentor (primary): owns daily syncs, code reviews, performance notes.
- Shadow hosts (2): 2-week rotations in adjacent teams/features to surface collaboration and product sense.
- Learning owner (optional): curates learning path and micro-project milestones.

Evaluation rubric (evidence-first, five areas). Each area scored 1-5 with explicit evidence notes (required):
1) Technical competence (core domain): Can complete assigned micro-project, demonstrates debugging and system thinking. Evidence: PRs, code review notes, failure postmortem.
2) Product judgement & impact: Recognizes trade-offs, suggests focused scope to ship. Evidence: demo narrative, feature prioritization discussion notes.
3) Collaboration & communication: Asks clear questions, responds to async threads, takes feedback. Evidence: Slack excerpts, peer review comments, cross-team pull requests.
4) Ramp velocity & autonomy: Time-to-first-meaningful-change and frequency of independent fixes. Evidence: timeline of tickets closed, ability to own a slice of feature.
5) Coachability & learning cadence: Absorbs feedback, iterates. Evidence: mentor notes, repeated improvement across sprints.

Scoring guidance (quick interpretation):
- 23-25: Strong conversion candidate, proceed to compensation calibration and offer draft.
- 18-22: Consider conversion with conditional development plan (probation-style goals).
- <=17: Not recommended for conversion; provide a growth plan and closure feedback.

Required artifacts for a conversion packet (submit to People Ops):
- Final demo video (5-8 mins) or live demo slot.
- Completed rubric with written evidence for each rubric item (2–5 bullet evidence points).
- Link to representative PR(s) and reviewer comments.
- Manager recommendation (yes/conditional/no) + compensation band request.

Decision timeline and cadence:
- After demo, panel meets within 5 business days to rate rubric.
- People Ops comp sync within 2 business days post-decision to prepare offer.
- Total decision-to-offer time target: <= 10 business days.

First 72-hour (faststart) checklist (concrete):
Day 0 (pre-join): share access checklist (email account, laptop image, Slack invites, intro reading pack).
Day 1:
- 09:00: Welcome quick sync (People Ops + manager) — 30m.
- 10:00: Mentor intro + codebase orientation — 60m.
- 14:00: Shadow rotation schedule review + set first micro-ticket.
- 16:00: Pairing with buddy to run local dev env and make first tiny commit.
Day 2:
- 10:00: Mini-sprint planning: define week-1 micro-deliverable.
- 15:00: Intro to product PR process and testing framework.
Day 3:
- 11:00: First async demo (screenshare + short writeup) to mentor; gather feedback.
- End of day: manager 1:1 to set expectations and core learning goals.

30-day activation milestones (illustrative):
- Week 1: environment + first commit; assigned learning modules completed.
- Week 2-3: Own a small end-to-end micro-feature (design -> tests -> PR -> deploy).
- Week 4: Cross-team shadow rotation + demo prep begins.
- End of month: Demo rehearsal, rubric pre-fill by mentor.

Hiring interview add-ons (if conversion proceeds to formal interview):
- Keep it light: one technical take-home (focused on relevant stack) + 2 behavioral interviews (manager & cross-functional).
- Use internal conversion packet as primary evidence; interviews validate fit for scale and compensation.

Risk & mitigation log (common traps):
- Low demo quality: mitigation = mandatory rehearsal slot + checklist for demos.
- Mentor bandwidth: mitigation = pre-assigned shadow hosts and time-blocked pairing hours.
- Decision delays: mitigation = hard calendar slots for panel and People Ops SLA.

Offer calibration notes (people ops):
- Use entry IC bands for interns converted in-cycle; add 1-level uplift for exceptional impact.
- Approvals: manager -> People Ops -> compensation committee for above-standard bands.

Communication templates (brief):
- Positive conversion: "Hi X — we’d love to extend an offer for a full-time IC role. Next steps..."
- Conditional conversion: "We recommend a conversion with a 90-day growth plan focused on Y. If targets are met, an offer will follow."
- Non-conversion: "We value your work; here are concrete areas to grow and alumni resources."

Appendix: suggested rubric notes format (copyable)
- Technical competence (4/5): "Completed micro-feature A; PR #123; mentor note: needed guidance on edge cases but debugged effectively."
- Product judgement (3/5): "Chose MVE but missed an opportunity to reduce scope earlier; demo narrative shows learning."

Next steps (for this doc):
- Validate with two hiring managers (Product infra + Console) and iterate rubric language.
- Pilot with next intern cohort (June intake) and collect metrics.
- After pilot, merge into canonical Confluence page and produce a lightweight training slide deck for mentors.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally concise and evidence-driven — feedback wanted on scoring thresholds, demo checklist, and People Ops SLA timings.
